text:
nora: Kickoff for airgap/operator-shim + customer-managed networking scoping. Goal: align upgrade lanes, offline bundle format, and network validation for customers who can't accept outbound connections.

ash: Important: airgap customers often have strict DNS split-horizon and BFD not configured. We need explicit checks and recommended defaults.

diego: Agreed. Also: the operator-shim must be able to apply delta bundles (patches) without full bundle swap. Full bundle swaps are heavy for constrained datacenters.

marta: Can you sketch what 'delta' means operationally?

diego: Delta = package with only changed images + manifest diff + signed checksum. Installer applies patch in place, verifies signatures, updates nodes rolling. For offline, checksum verification must work entirely locally.

nora: Proposed CLI options for airgap:
```
redwood-install --mode onprem --airgap /path/to/bundle.tar.gz --network customer-managed --dns-mode split-horizon
```
CLI should run offline preflight (no outbound) and produce an artifacts report with checksums and an action plan.

ash: Preflight items to include: manifest signature verification, node diskspace, iptables/SNAT detection, DNS resolution for controlplane VIP (local check), BFD session health (if configured), and operator-shim compatibility check.

marta: For BFD, recommend default timers tuned for datacenter hardware. Document fallback to static route polling when BFD not present.

diego: Rollout lanes idea:
- Lane 1 (Airgap light): small customers w/ relay or NAT-preserve; accept delta patches; minimal BGP/BFD requirements.
- Lane 2 (Airgap std): certified BGP peering, BFD optional but recommended, full egress preservation. Requires lab pass.
- Lane 3 (Enterprise): certified BGP+BFD, route filtering, audit logs, contract SOW for IP retention, and two production pilots.

nora: Good. For upgrades: define two upgrade types: patch (delta) and major (bundle upgrade). Patch should support rolling in-place with 0-5min token-level degradation and ability to abort. Major requires canary + staged rollout across tenants/nodes with telemetry rollback triggers.

ash: Telemetry triggers: controlplane handshake latency > 2x baseline OR KV-store write latency spike OR failed healthcheck rate > 1%. We'll tie these into automatic pause/rollback. Need infra hooks.

marta: Also add a conservative backoff for retrying network BGP sessions to avoid flapping during upgrades.

diego: Airgap verification plan: produce an "audit manifest" artifact that includes all checksums, expected egress IPs, and a validated preflight log. This artifact should be part of customer delivery and signed by us.

nora: Legal/customer ask: some customers request explicit IP preservation language. Suggest: we offer a "Preserved-Egress" SOW addendum with operational requirements (fixed CIDR, no dynamic NATing during maintenance window) and a tested rollback play.

ash: If we sign IP retention, ops needs the right to schedule maintenance windows and an emergency rollback SLA. Add to SOW draft.

marta: Pilot criteria: for Lane2->Lane3 promo, require at least one pilot in a cloud-proximate datacenter and one in a strict airgapped colo, both passing e2e peering and delta patch tests.

diego: Implementation ask: infra needs a library to create/verify signed manifests and a staging lab harness that can simulate split-horizon DNS and enforced SNAT. This is ~3w effort.

nora: Timeline: if infra can deliver the manifest tooling + preflight checks in 3w, Product proposes an initial Lane1 GA 1w after that + pilot week. So ~4w total for Lane1. Lane2/3 depend on lab runs and pilots (additional 4-6w).

infra-bot: New ticket created: OFFLINE-2217 "signed-manifest-and-airgap-preflight" assigned to infra.

ash: Action items:
- diego: prototype delta bundle format and signed manifest (due +12d)
- ash: preflight checklist doc + DNS/BFD guidance (due +10d)
- marta: SOW language draft for Preserved-Egress and maintenance windows (due +14d)
- nora: coordinate pilot candidates and draft lane definitions for launch gating (due +10d)

diego: I'll include sample delta layout and a small CLI snip for local verification. Example diff check: 
```
# verify manifest signatures
redwood-verify --manifest audit.json --key redwood.pub
# apply delta (dry-run)
redwood-install --apply-delta delta.tar.gz --dry-run
```

marta: One more ops constraint: for customers running strict FIPS/HSM, the signed manifest step needs to support customer-supplied HSM keys for verification. Add to backlog.

nora: Thanks all. We'll reconvene in engineering sync after diego's prototype lands. Keep messages short on this thread.

ash: +1, thanks."
